title.narrative: FAN/RAISG Amazonas vatten sårbarhet för klimatförändringar och föroreningar
FAN/RAISG: Amazon water vulnerability to climate change and pollution

description.narrative:
Målet med projektet är att skydda och återställa vattenresurser och akvatiska ekosystem i Amazonas som är sårbara och löper hög risk för nedbrytning som en prioritet för att garantera dess invånare en säker och motståndskraftig framtid mot effekterna av klimatförändringarna, vilket bidrar till de globala målen.
De fyra specifika målen för projektet är att: 1. Generera georefererade data om den faktiska sårbarheten hos Amazonas ytvatten för klimatförändringar, markanvändning och förorening för att vägleda beslutsfattande och öka medvetenheten hos myndigheter och vattenförvaltningsinstitutioner i Amazonas länder och den allmänna opinionen om : Vattensäkerhet enligt inverkan på hydrologiska resurser baserat på torka, översvämningar, hydrologiskt arbete och vattenföroreningar i olika geografiska enheter (vattendelar, avdelningar, kommuner, inhemska territorier, skyddade områden, Ramsar-områden). Nedbrytning av vattenförekomster och vattenkällor genom förorening som härrör från verksamheten inom gruvdrift, urbanisering, jordbruk och andra påfrestningar med deras åtföljande risker för levnadsmedlen i Amazonas samhällen och biologisk mångfald. 2. Övervaka processerna kopplade till vattnets kretslopp och förvaltning i Amazonas, främja allianser/synergier med institutioner och observatorier, privata företag och andra, för att stödja upprättandet av ett regionalt nätverk för mätning av indikatorer för effekter på vattenproduktivitet i vad gäller kvalitet och kvantitet i de olika länderna med sikte på en hållbar framtid. 3. Främja tekniska samarbetsåtgärder genom dialoger om vattenfrågor i Amazonas för att ge input till politik och vattenskyddsåtgärder baserade på ny kunskap och behovet av att uppfylla målen för hållbar utveckling 6 (Vatten), 13 (Klimatförändringar) och 15 (Liv på land). 4. Stärka samarbetet mellan de åtta icke-statliga Amazon-organisationerna som utgör RAISG och implementera en ny förvaltningsmodell för att övervaka och främja en integrerad vision för Amazonas organisationer med det gemensamma målet att skydda den stora socio-miljömässiga och kulturella biologiska mångfalden.

The goal of the project is to value, protect, and restore water resources and aquatic ecosystems in the Amazon that are vulnerable and at high risk of degradation as a priority to guarantee its inhabitants a safe and resilient water future to the effects of climate change, contributing to the Sustainable Development objectives of the agenda 2030.
The four specific objectives of the project are to: 1. Generate georeferenced data about the actual vulnerability of the surface water of the Amazon for climate change, land use, and contamination to guide decision­making and increase awareness on the part of the authorities and water management institutions of the Amazon countries and the public opinion on:­ Water security according to the impact on hydrological resources based on droughts, flooding, hydrological work, and water pollution in different geographical units (watersheds, departments, municipalities, indigenous territories, protected areas, Ramsar sites). ­ Degradation of bodies and sources of water by contamination derived from the activities of mining, urbanization, agriculture and other pressures with their consequent risks for the means of life of the Amazon communities and biodiversity. 2. Monitor the processes linked to the water cycle and management in the Amazon, promoting alliances/synergias with institutions and observatories, private companies, and others, to support the establishment of a regional network for the measurement of indicators of impacts on water productivity in terms of quality and quantity in the different countries with a view towards a sustainable future. 3. Promote technical cooperation actions through dialogues on water issues in the Amazon to provide inputs to policies and water protection measures based on new knowledge and the need to fulfill the Sustainable Development Goals 6 (Water), 13 (Climate Change) and 15 (Life on Land). 4. Strengthen the cooperative work between the eight Amazon non-governmental organisations composing RAISG and implement a new governance model to monitor and promote an integrated vision for the Amazon organizations with the common goal of protecting the great socio­environmental and cultural biodiversity.

The goal of the project is to value, protect, and restore water resources and aquatic ecosystems in the Amazon that are vulnerable and at high risk of degradation as a priority to guarantee its inhabitants a safe and resilient water future to the effects of climate change, contributing to the Sustainable Development objectives of the agenda 2030.
The four specific objectives of the project are to:
1. Generate georeferenced data about the actual vulnerability of the surface water of the Amazon for climate change, land use, and contamination to guide decision-making and increase awareness on the part of the authorities and water management institutions of the Amazon countries and the public opinion on:
- Water security according to the impact on hydrological resources based on droughts, flooding, hydrological work, and water pollution in different geographical units (watersheds, departments, municipalities, indigenous territories, protected areas, Ramsar sites).
- Degradation of bodies and sources of water by contamination derived from the activities of mining, urbanization, agriculture and other pressures with their consequent risks for the means of life of the Amazon communities and biodiversity.
2. Monitor the processes linked to the water cycle and management in the Amazon, promoting alliances/synergias with institutions and observatories, private companies, and others, to support the establishment of a regional network for the measurement of indicators of impacts on water productivity in terms of quality and quantity in the different countries with a view towards a sustainable future.
3. Promote technical cooperation actions through dialogues on water issues in the Amazon to provide inputs to policies and water protection measures based on new knowledge and the need to fulfill the Sustainable Development Goals 6 (Water), 13 (Climate Change) and 15 (Life on Land).
4. Strengthen the cooperative work between the eight Amazon non governmental organisations composing RAISG and implement a new governance model to monitor and promote an integrated vision for the Amazon organizations with the common goal of protecting the great socio-environmental and cultural biodiversity.
This project is mainly linked to three of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) established by the UN in Agenda 2030 namely: Goal 6 - Guarantee the availability of water and sustainable management and sanitation for all; Goal 13 - Adopt urgent measures to combat climate change and its effects; and, Goal 15 - Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss.

PERIOD 1: DEC/2023 to NOV/2024
Period 1 of the contribution was divided in two phases. The first semester allowed RAISG and its eight member organisations to do an inception that served as input to rearrange and further develop the interventions theory of change and approach. During the second semester, the proposed activities were initiated.
RAISGs operations during Period 1 have led to advancements in addressing water vulnerability in the Amazon. By adopting a comprehensive watershed perspective, the organization has been able to analyze water quality and the impacts of contamination more effectively. This approach has fostered synergy and coordination with other initiatives such as MapBiomas Agua and Wetlands, allowing for the exchange of experiences and methodologies. As a result, technical information on the current and future state of Amazonian water bodies, rivers, and wetlands has been strengthened, especially in light of increasing pressures and threats to these ecosystems.
According to the results of mapping the vulnerability of water bodies, Colombia is the most affected country, with water bodies shrinking by 13% in the last decade. Similarly, Suriname and Bolivia have seen their water bodies shrink by 9% and 8% respectively. With regards to water pollution, 30 pilot monitoring sites were prioritized in the different Amazon countries. The water quality assessment was carried out in the second half of the first year of the project in the Amazon of Peru and Bolivia; in the rest of the countries, it will be carried out in year 2.
One of the changes has been the establishment of collaborative frameworks within RAISG. These have enabled common agreements for field interventions and the development of water quality assessments in priority pilot sites across different countries. Through this collaboration, key indicators and parameters have been defined to evaluate the ecological health of Amazonian rivers and watersheds, e.g., intensification of mining river sediments, fish muscle and aquatic diversity to measure mercury contamination.
Additionally, the incorporation of a gender and rights approach has changed institutional attitudes and behaviors. A formal agreement now promotes gender equity and the inclusion of diverse groups in RAISGs policies and actions, based on a diagnosis of opportunities and actions carried out by partner institutions.
The target groupsRAISG members, local actors, and partner institutionsare now capable of conducting coordinated water quality assessments using standardized methodologies. They are also better equipped to engage in joint advocacy efforts and influence decision-makers. This marks a shift from the beginning of the intervention, where such coordination and inclusivity were less developed.
Furthermore, the operations have made a difference by enhancing regional collaboration and technical capacity. Strategic alliances have been formed with key stakeholders such as the Scientific Panel for the Amazon (SPA), Amazonian Waters (WCS), the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), and the North Amazonian Alliance (ANA). These efforts were further amplified at COP16 on biodiversity, where RAISG, alongside the Amazon Initiative 80x2025, issued an urgent call to prevent reaching the point of no return and emphasized the recognition of indigenous territories in biodiversity protection.
In summary, RAISGs interventions have not only improved the technical and collaborative landscape for water governance in the Amazon but have also fostered inclusive and impactful advocacy, making a difference in the regions environmental and social resilience.
